hook.text: Andrew Carnegie built 2,509 libraries worldwide. He also crushed unions and paid steelworkers starvation wages.

buildup.text: Philanthropy has always served dual purposes: genuine altruism and strategic reputation laundering.

discovery.text: The 'Giving Pledge' asks billionaires to donate half their wealth. Over 200 have signed—but few have delivered.

twist.text: Effective altruism argues most philanthropy is wasteful. A malaria net saves more lives per dollar than an opera house.

climax.text: Tax deductions turn charity into a profitable activity. The giver saves money while choosing where public funds go.

punchline.text: Generosity and self-interest share more DNA than we admit.

quiz.question: How many libraries did Andrew Carnegie build?
